review.rationale: Engineering review of this explicitly hashed measurement: the same-runtime v2 bitidentity test is not satisfied across the upstream Torch/vLLM upgrade and remains a failed recorded check. On unchanged stored BF16 references, short PPL improves 0.125% and 32K-suffix PPL 0.321%; short JS, reverse KL and KL tails improve. Mean short KL increases 0.000872 and long KL 0.000129. BF16-relative top1 agreement changes from 492/512 to 490/512 short probes and stays 8/8 long probes. These are mixed distribution changes, not a claim of identical output or a general quality improvement. Independently referenced kernel math and all four actual-state replay cases pass the unchanged tolerances, including full-graph C4 and long prefill. Accept the bounded upgrade numerics with these explicit limitations; no attention tolerance was relaxed.
review.limits: Finite engineered panels; stored references reused without executing old runtime or original BF16 model. Old and new isolated JIT caches can produce different floating-point execution choices; cause of every cross-version token difference is not proven. API, resource and performance gates are still required.

stored_v2.scope: Fresh candidate short panel plus first existing 32K-prefix suffix window. Long numerical attention/graph tolerances are separately checked by matched-state replay; not a new broad quality campaign.

quality_measurements.scope: New Torch/vLLM changes cannot be approved by the old same-runtime bitidentity check. The failed old check remains evidence; review these differences together with unchanged FP32/native kernel and actual-state numerical gates. No old runtime was executed.

limitations: Full-reference output distributions change across Torch/vLLM versions; old bitidentity gate failed and is retained, not relabeled. New-image numerical gates retain original tolerances.
Frozen finite quality panels and state probes cannot guarantee identical generated text or all-task accuracy.
Official upstream dependency metadata conflicts are inherited unchanged; actual GPU ABI and serving tests qualify this exact stack.
Clean C4 and maximum single context are separate from C16 pressure, which permits recorded preemptions.
DFlash, old-runtime inference and old-baseline benchmark reruns were excluded.
